title: Hotel Accused of Canceling Conference for NBA Finals Business
summary: A lawsuit over a hotel's alleged decision to replace a longstanding conference with higher-value NBA Finals business has been settled. But the dispute exposed a contract vulnerability many planners still overlook.

title: What’s Behind Forrester’s Pivot to Smaller Events
summary: The research firm is betting big on shorter, more intimate forums to reverse a 57% decline in event revenue over three years.

title: Gendered Ageism: The Events Industry’s Chronic Issue
summary: Women event professionals report being stereotyped, harassed, unable to balance work and family, paid less than men, and then as the ultimate insult, forced out of their jobs at the late stage of their careers. And that’s in an industry made up mostly of women.

title: AI Stand-Ins Are Reshaping the Economics of Virtual Events
summary: Not all attendees at virtual meetings are human. AI note-taking bots are proliferating, and although they may assist attendees with note-taking and summaries, they are posing challenges for planners.

title: 8 Places to Find Inspiration for Your Events
summary: Creativity is rarely a straight line — it’s an exploration. This is where planners get fresh ideas for their events.

title: Conference Ejections Trigger ADA Leadership Shake-Up and Internal Review
summary: The issue wasn't whether the ADA could enforce its rules. It was whether the organization's response, including the involvement of law enforcement, became a bigger story than the violation itself.

title: World Cup's Triple Threat: Security, Heat, and Disease
summary: Though organizers have announced strategies for every possible contingency, from drone attacks to food poisoning — the biggest of all is the weather.

title: Bali’s New Convention Center Ups the Ante for Large Groups
summary: One of the most popular resort destinations in Southeast Asia, Bali has a new option for large-scale meetings.

title: These Smaller Cities Are Pouring Billions Into Convention Centers
summary: Convention center investment is no longer concentrated in a handful of first-tier cities; cities from Albany to Indianapolis are spending billions to compete for meetings business. They are betting that modern facilities and walkable districts will draw planners in.

title: Is Charging for No Shows a Bad Idea?
summary: Some companies have had it with no-shows and started charging a penalty. Others say that only makes them a target on social media.
